headline: High: OpenBBTerminal’s MCP/API surfaces can ingest Botpress outputs, creating default-path prompt-injection and cascading-action risk; compliance risk is medium due to financial-data handling.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Botpress is a chatbot agent and OpenBBTerminal exposes MCP/REST/FastAPI surfaces, so a plausible bridge exists if Botpress outputs are routed into OpenBB inputs. The profiles do not document a shared channel or default ingestion, so I cannot justify high; uncertainty pushes to medium rather than low because the interaction is plausible and OpenBB’s MCP surface is explicit.
conditions: IF Botpress messages are forwarded into OpenBBTerminal via MCP, REST, or stdin/stdout
IF OpenBBTerminal treats Botpress-generated text as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Disable any Botpress-to-OpenBB forwarding path
Require strict schema validation on all Botpress-originated payloads
Add a provenance tag and reject untrusted instruction-like fields
Use a separate workspace or process boundary for the two agents
requires-engineering: insert an allowlist parser between Botpress and OpenBB

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenBBTerminal touches financial, licensed, and public data, while Botpress is a customer-support agent that may handle user content. OpenBB exposes APIs and MCP servers, so if Botpress can pass context into those interfaces, sensitive data could leak across the pair. The profiles do not show shared storage or direct exfiltration, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF Botpress forwards customer content into OpenBBTerminal requests
IF OpenBBTerminal logs or returns that content through its API/MCP responses
mitigations: Strip secrets and PII before any Botpress-to-OpenBB call
Turn off verbose request/response logging
Use separate credentials for each agent
Review MCP tool schemas for data-minimizing fields
requires-engineering: add DLP filtering on the integration boundary

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Botpress can install packages, while OpenBBTerminal cannot write files, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses, so direct write-write conflict is limited. OpenBB does support multiple instances and MCP/API access, but the profiles do not show overlapping mutable filesystem or git scopes. The main conflict is operational rather than destructive, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable project directory
IF Botpress package installation changes the runtime environment used by OpenBBTerminal
mitigations: Run each agent in a separate virtual environment
Pin dependencies for Botpress
Keep OpenBBTerminal read-only to shared assets
Avoid sharing a writable working directory
requires-engineering: add filesystem isolation between runtimes

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenBBTerminal’s API/MCP surfaces can consume upstream inputs, and Botpress is a conversational agent whose outputs may be treated as actionable text. If OpenBB uses Botpress output without verification, errors can cascade into financial-modeling outputs or downstream actions. The profiles do not prove automatic action-taking, so medium is the safest choice.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal consumes Botpress output as authoritative input
IF no human or programmatic verification step checks Botpress-derived facts before use
mitigations: Require human review before acting on Botpress-derived outputs
Add a verification step against primary financial sources
Mark Botpress outputs as untrusted in the integration layer
Limit Botpress to drafting, not executing, OpenBB workflows
requires-engineering: implement confidence and provenance checks

E_compliance.rationale: OpenBBTerminal explicitly touches financial and licensed data, while Botpress is a customer-support agent with no documented residency or retention controls in the profile. That creates a plausible compliance mismatch if support content and financial data are combined or retained together. I do not see evidence of PHI or a specific residency violation, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF customer-support content from Botpress is stored alongside OpenBB financial or licensed data
IF retention or deletion policies differ across the two systems
mitigations: Separate support and financial datasets
Document retention periods for each system
Restrict access to licensed data exports
Review whether any support transcripts contain regulated data
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows
